## Before you upgrade

- **Run the agent install line once more.** The 0.3.0, 0.3.1 and 0.3.2 agent programs trust a release key whose private half was lost (it is now revoked), so they cannot check the 0.3.3 agents and keep running the version they have. On each computer, run the install line from **Add data** again to move it to 0.3.3. From 0.3.3 on, agent programs are signed with the new release key and agents update themselves when the server is upgraded. See [Key management](https://signalith.io/docs/key-management/).
- **Upgrade every server of a cluster before attaching files to cases.** A server still on 0.3.2 or older that changes a case drops which file each of its file entries names, and those files are then deleted at the next retention run.
- **Compliance scores may go down.** Response actions, notifications, user accounts and asset lists now count as evidence only once they are shown to work, not as soon as they are set up (see Fixes). (COMP-02)
- **A new install of the bundled OpenSearch needs about 4 GB of memory.** On a smaller computer, `signalith opensearch install` and the `.msi` stop unless you choose a heap with `-heap` (`OPENSEARCHHEAP` for the `.msi`). Upgrades only warn. See [OpenSearch's memory](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#opensearchs-memory).
- **Subsearches take up to 10,000 events.** A plain event search inside `join`, `append`, `union`, `multisearch` or `set` used to take only the newest 100 events without saying so. It now takes up to **Events per search** (Settings > Search) and is marked Sampled when more match, so saved searches and detections built on them can return more rows. That setting now goes up to 10,000, the most OpenSearch returns; a higher value in `signalith.yaml` is used as 10,000 and logged at startup. (SL-101, SL-102)
- **Scheduled snapshots need the snapshot role given once.** Signalith is no longer given the `signalith_snapshots` role (which lets it take and delete snapshots) until you want scheduled snapshots. Docker quick start: `snapshot.sh register` gives it, and an update keeps it where a snapshot repository or Signalith's snapshot policy exists. Helm: set `opensearch.snapshotRole: true`. `signalith opensearch install`: run `signalith opensearch snapshot-role on`. An install from before keeps the role it had: if you don't use scheduled snapshots, run `signalith opensearch snapshot-role off` once, as an administrator, to take it away. The Health page says when it is missing. See [Scheduled snapshots](https://signalith.io/docs/backup/#what-opensearch-needs). (CM-107)

## What's new

- **Each computer gets a key of its own.** The Signalith Agent now trades its install line's token for a key that holds for its computer only, the first time it talks to the server, and sends with it from then on. One computer can be cut off with `signalith tokens hosts revoke <name>`, and a computer of a line can no longer report as another one that has its key. Agents update to it by themselves; nothing to do. A computer installed again under the same name needs `signalith tokens hosts release <name>` once. See [Computer keys](https://signalith.io/docs/agent-tokens/#computer-keys). (ASI-102)
- **Case templates, tasks and files.** Open a case from a template with its task checklist, and attach files (up to 10 MiB each) with their SHA-256. Files are only ever downloaded. See [Investigations](https://signalith.io/docs/cases/#attaching-files). (AW-2)
- **Signed case reports.** **Export** on a case downloads a report page or JSON, signed with the server's report key. **Check a report** on the Investigations page and `signalith report verify` check the signature, the evidence and the page. See [Exporting a report](https://signalith.io/docs/cases/#exporting-a-report). (AW-2)
- **Compliance evidence history.** On the first day of each month, Signalith records every framework's score and each control's status, signed with the server's report key, and admins can take a record at any time. The Compliance page's **History** tab lists them and says whether each still checks out, so you can show the evidence held all along. See [Evidence history](https://signalith.io/docs/compliance/#evidence-history). (AW-15)
- **An Industrial protocols option for the network sensor.** A tick box when setting up a new sensor (`--ot` on the install line): Suricata parses Modbus, DNP3 and EtherNet/IP, and Zeek gets CISA's ICSNPP analyzers, each pinned to a commit and built on the sensor. The sensor still only listens. See [Industrial protocols](https://signalith.io/docs/network-sensor/#industrial-protocols).
- **Scheduled snapshots.** Turn on **Scheduled snapshots** in **Settings > Server > Backups** and OpenSearch snapshots Signalith's indices on a schedule (every day at 02:30 by default) and keeps the last 14, leaving out days in cold storage (they live in their own snapshots), through an OpenSearch snapshot management policy that the server running the background jobs keeps. The **Health** page gets a **Backups** card with the last and next snapshot and the last `signalith backup` of the server's files, and a red item when the last successful snapshot is more than two periods old. The quick start's OpenSearch roles gain `signalith_snapshots`; on your own OpenSearch, add it as [Scheduled snapshots](https://signalith.io/docs/backup/#scheduled-snapshots) shows. A [restore drill](https://signalith.io/docs/backup/#restore-drill) covers one server and a cluster. (SS-14)
- **One command sets up OpenSearch on Linux.** After installing the package, `sudo signalith opensearch install` downloads OpenSearch 3.9.0 for Linux (x64 or arm64), checks it against the SHA-512 Signalith pins, runs it as the `signalith-opensearch` systemd service on this server only, over HTTPS with no passwords, and points Signalith at it with a certificate. See [OpenSearch on Linux](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#opensearch-on-linux). (OB-3)

- **Metrics for Prometheus.** `GET /metrics` answers each server's ingest, OpenSearch, syslog, retention and job numbers in the Prometheus or OpenMetrics format. It is off until an admin turns it on in **Settings > Metrics** and makes a scrape token, which is shown once; scrapes must come over HTTPS or from the server itself, and are rate limited. See [Metrics for Prometheus](https://signalith.io/docs/metrics/). (SS-05)
- **Choose the bundled OpenSearch's memory.** `signalith opensearch install` and `adopt` take `-heap` (such as `4g`), and the `.msi` takes `OPENSEARCHHEAP`. Upgrades and repairs keep it. See [OpenSearch's memory](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#opensearchs-memory). (WIN-05)
- **Helm: an Ingress and an agent Service.** `ingress.enabled` adds an Ingress for the web page, and `server.agentService` adds a LoadBalancer Service for the agent port alone. Both are off by default. See [Kubernetes](https://signalith.io/docs/kubernetes/#exposing-signalith). (DEP-03)
- **Detection content refresh.** The SigmaHQ pack now has 2,641 rules and the Splunk pack 1,332, with upstream edits to 18 Sigma and 11 Splunk rules.
- **Checking a download names the exact signer.** The release's GPG key fingerprint is published in SECURITY.md, the README and the install docs, and the Sigstore and attestation checks name the release workflow at the tag. The apt and dnf repositories are built only from packages whose build provenance checks out. See [Check a download](https://signalith.io/docs/install-packages/#check-a-download). (SSD-03, SSD-06, SSD-08)
- **Turn off the built-in admin.** Once another admin account exists, an admin can turn the built-in admin off on the Users page, which ends its sessions and refuses its password, passkeys and Basic credentials, with an audit record. `signalith passwd` on a server turns it back on if every admin is locked out. On several servers, every server must be on 0.3.3 first. The Security page recommends it. See [Turning the built-in admin off](https://signalith.io/docs/users/#turning-the-built-in-admin-off).
- **Find events dated by their sender.** When an event's own time is more than 5 minutes from when it arrived, the arrival is stored in `signalith_received` (as Splunk's `_indextime`), so `signalith_received=*` finds backdated or postdated events. (RTINGEST-101)
**Signalith Agent**
- **Signed agent updates.** The agent programs in this release are signed with a new release key, so agents installed from 0.3.3 update themselves to later releases again. See [Key management](https://signalith.io/docs/key-management/).
- **Staged agent updates.** **Update first** in **Endpoints > What hosts collect** sends a new agent version to 1 in 10, a quarter or half of an install line's computers, always the same ones, before the rest. An update that was undone is tried again a day later. (ASI-07)
- **An alert for a silent agent.** A computer whose Signalith Agent sends nothing for an hour now raises a finding (the new built-in detection *Signalith Agent silent*), as a silent network sensor already did. **Alert when silent** in **Endpoints > What hosts collect** sets how long each install line may stay quiet, or turns it off. (ASI-14)
- **The agent checks the Fluent Bit configuration it is handed.** It refuses one that would run a program, load a plugin, open a port, read a file holding secrets or send anywhere but its own Signalith server, keeps the configuration in use, and still takes the rest of the configuration, agent updates included. Only settings Signalith writes are allowed, and the configuration on disk is checked again at startup. (ASI-03)
- **Windows on ARM.** The install line now sets up the agent on Windows 11 on ARM (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs). The agent runs as an ARM program, with the x86 Fluent Bit and osquery Windows runs on ARM, and Sysmon's ARM build. Servers hand out the new `signalith-agent-windows-arm64.exe`, and the manual Fluent Bit steps now say to use the win64 installer on ARM PCs, since Fluent Bit's ARM build 5.1.3 crashes as it starts sending.

**Network sensor**
- **Sensors keep their agent configuration up to date.** Every hour a sensor asks Signalith for its Fluent Bit configuration again and, when it changed, checks it and restarts Fluent Bit with it, so a new release's sensor logs reach every sensor without running the line again. Only reading the sensor's own logs and sending to the same server and certificate authority is allowed; anything else is refused and the configuration in use kept. See [The agent's configuration](https://signalith.io/docs/network-sensor/#the-agents-configuration). (DEP-06)

**Vulnerabilities**
- **Version-only matches on distribution packages.** CVEs matched by version alone on software a Linux distribution built (the banner names Ubuntu, Debian, Red Hat and others, which fix CVEs without changing the version) are marked **Version only** on the Vulnerabilities page and `vuln_confidence=version_only` in their events, and no longer raise the critical and likely exploited detections. Known exploited ones still do. (ASI-02)
- **CVEs from installed packages.** Linux hosts that run osquery now list their deb and rpm packages every 6 hours, and Signalith matches them to their distribution's advisories from OSV.dev (Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux), comparing versions as `dpkg` and `rpm` do. A CVE is reported only when the installed version is older than the version the distribution fixed it in. Results show under **Installed packages** on the Vulnerabilities page and as events with `vuln_confidence=package`, and raise the known exploited, critical and likely exploited detections. Only the releases your hosts run are downloaded, once a day; set **Distribution advisories address** to a mirror, a folder or `off`. See [Installed packages](https://signalith.io/docs/vulnerabilities/#installed-packages-on-linux-hosts). (ASI-19, ASI-02)

**Several servers**
- **Several servers is a preview.** The [Servers](https://signalith.io/docs/servers/) and [Adding servers](https://signalith.io/docs/multi-server/) pages now say so: it is tested in CI and the lab but is newer than the rest of Signalith, and one server stays the recommended setup in the 0.x releases.

## Fixes

**Signalith server**
- **The installer warns when the disk is nearly full.** Setting up OpenSearch now says so when its disk will be more than 85% full. Above 90% OpenSearch creates no new indexes, so Signalith cannot store events. The warning says how much room to free.
- **Setting up OpenSearch says it is still starting.** Its first start can take a few minutes, during which the installer used to show nothing after "Starting OpenSearch...". It now says how long it waits (up to 5 minutes) and prints a line every 30 seconds until OpenSearch answers.
- Batches that agents send at the same time are written to OpenSearch together. Many agents each sending a small batch every second made many small writes, each spread over every index its events belong to, and the disk syncs per write capped how many events a second were stored: about 1,050 a second of real Windows events on the cloud test lab's two OpenSearch servers. The same lab now stores about 3,260 a second.
- **The audit integrity check notices a deleted past month.** It used to treat only the current month as undeletable, so removing a whole earlier month's audit index looked clean. Every month that the audit category's `keep_days` keeps must now hold a signed record of the servers that sign theirs, or the check reports it removed. (SCC-04)
- **`signalith security` no longer assumes the service can't be dumped.** It used to report the memory check Good from the core limit alone; it now reads whether the running service is dumpable, and for one running as root claims only the core limit. In a container, a core limit it couldn't read no longer counts as "no crash dumps". (SEC-04)
- The Servers page no longer warns on the 1st and 2nd of each month that OpenSearch will run out of shards because of the new month's audit index: that index is added once a month, not every day kept.
- Cloud and identity rules in the SigmaHQ pack (AWS, Azure and Entra ID, Google Cloud, GitHub, Kubernetes, Microsoft 365, Okta) are now titled for the account (`... for $user$`), keep one finding a day per account, address and action rather than one per account, and put risk on the account and the address instead of the Collector that read the log. (DQ-04)
- **Sampled results are marked everywhere.** Dashboard panels, notebook cells, searches saved to a case and a detection's **Last run** now say when the commands after the search ran over only the newest events, as the Search page already did. A scheduled rule like `eval ... | stats count` that counted only the newest 10,000 events now says so, and the server logs a warning. (SL-01)
- **Pages say plainly when OpenSearch is down.** Dashboard cards and panels, notebook searches and error replies now say OpenSearch is not answering and point to the Health page, instead of showing its address and the raw connection error. The sample data card says why it could not check, the setup guide keeps trying for a few minutes instead of not opening, and the Health page gives advice for a refused connection. (OB-6)

- **Detections no longer stop after OpenSearch restarts.** While OpenSearch was starting, a read of the shared settings could look as if they had been deleted, and the server stopped running detections until it was restarted. Such a read now keeps the server's copy until OpenSearch answers.
- OpenVAS findings without a CVE are throttled per finding, so a second one on the same host is no longer held back for a week by the first.
- `signalith cluster accept-restore` no longer fails when a running server writes its own settings at the same moment.
- `signalith reset-key` warns that the cluster's CA key is lost too, and says so afterwards.
- Settings tabs wrap on wide screens and fade at the edge on phones.
- **OTLP requests are capped.** Each attribute list in an OTLP request keeps at most 256 attributes, a resource stops being copied into an event once it is full, and a request whose records come to more than 64 MB is refused with 413. A small request with a large resource could make the server use hundreds of megabytes. (SI-101)
- Adding a finding to a case now records its first response, so its SLA, the **Due** filter and the late-escalation rule no longer treat it as late. (AW-101)
- Compliance: the data retention control is Partial while events older than the retention setting are still stored, and NIST AU-9, GDPR 5(1)(f) and ISO A.8.15 cap at Partial, since OpenSearch does not make stored events immutable. (COMP-102, COMP-103)
- The **Health** page warns when scheduled snapshots are off and the server's files had no `signalith backup` in 30 days. (CM-108)
- Sigma rules on the Windows Security and System logs throttle on the event, account and what changed, so one finding for a service install or a logon no longer holds back every other one on that host for a day. (DQ-102)
- A subsearch written as `[* inputlookup...]` no longer turns into an unknown command.
**Signalith Agent**
- The agent's Fluent Bit configuration check refuses a section that sets `Name` (or another checked setting) twice. Fluent Bit runs the first `Name` and the check read the last, so a forbidden plugin could pass. (ASI-101)
- **The Linux install line no longer stops Fluent Bit or osquery you already run.** If `fluent-bit` (or, with `--osquery`, `osqueryd`) already runs on the computer, sending somewhere else say, the script now stops before changing anything and says so, instead of masking it without a word. Add `--take-over` to the line to stop and mask it anyway; `--uninstall` starts it again. (DEP-05)
- **Compliance evidence needs use, not only setup.** Response actions, notifications, user accounts and the asset lists were shown as evidence as soon as they were set up. Each is now partial until it is shown to work: a response action run that succeeded in the last 90 days, a notification delivered in the last 30 days with no failing channel, a named user who signed in in the last 90 days, and an asset or identity with an owner or a priority. Scores on servers that only set these up go down. (COMP-02)
- **Rules that need a GeoIP database stay off until there is one.** Turning on a rule that runs `iplocation` on a server with no GeoIP database now says why it cannot, and **Turn on all shown rules** leaves such rules off and says how many, instead of turning on rules whose every run fails. (DQ-03)
- **Free-text search explains words that find nothing.** When a search with a plain word matches nothing, the Search page now says a word matches whole words and the start of names such as `mimikatz.exe`, and suggests `*word*` to find it inside a word, instead of only suggesting a longer time range. (LP-04)

**Network sensor**
- The sensor install line tries `apt-get update` three times before it stops, so a package mirror that is mid-sync no longer stops the install.
